column14: Dailymotion may receive orders from authorities in European Member States to act against illegal content. In such an event, Dailymotion reviews in priority the content included in the order to verify if it violates our Prohibited Content Policy. If it does, we remove such content. Otherwise, Dailymotion may decide to restrict access to the content in the jurisdiction where it is alleged to be unlawful, after ensuring that the order is valid. During the reporting period, Dailymotion did not receive any orders from competent authorities in any Member State of the European Union to act against illegal content, such as law enforcement agencies (LEAs) or governments. The data presented in column G reflects the above statement.
column18: Dailymotion may receive requests from European Member States’ authorities for information about our service recipients during investigations. In such cases, Dailymotion verifies the legitimacy and legal validity of the request. If we doubt the request's authenticity or legitimacy, we may reject it or seek additional information.
column19: We receive requests from authorities through two channels: (1) a dedicated email address and (2) through the legal department. Requests sent to the dedicated email address benefit from a more efficient processing time due to an established dedicated process and automatic acknowledgment of receipt. In contrast, requests addressed to the legal department may take longer to process and do not have an automatic acknowledgment system. We strive to respond as quickly as possible with the requested information. The information provided here corresponds to the acknowledgement of receipt sent when requests are sent through the dedicated email address. For requests sent to the legal department, the acknowledgement of receipt is the same as the median time to give effect to the order.
column20:

Requests sent through the dedicated email address are handled more quickly than those sent to the legal department. This difference is due to several factors: (1) the dedicated email address has an on-duty system ensuring immediate attention, whereas the legal department does not. (2) When requests are sent to the legal department, they require extra processing steps, which add delays to the overall response time. Using the designated funnel ensures the most efficient processing of requests. 
Furthermore, information requests typically take longer to process as our teams must consult with another department than the receiving ones. Hence, longer turnaround times are to be expected.

column5: In this category, we list the notifications (i.e., user or trusted flagger reports) and sanctions (i.e., negative moderation decisions) that fall under our  “Child abuse” policy. We define child abuse as any behavior, action, or content that depicts, promotes, glorifies, or trivializes the physical, emotional, or psychological harm, neglect, or exploitation of children (individuals under 18 years old). This includes (1) Child labor, (2) Glorification or mockery, (3) Hoaxes, pranks, and dangerous challenges, (4) Bullying
